steps.content: One week ago.
Helga, the current Speaker of the Farland Assembly, sat across from you. She watched you with a warm smile and a steady gaze.
Strictly speaking, it was not a formal interrogation. After all, a Sinner had rarely voluntarily taken that seat to ask for help.
Helga had come alone, and for one purpose only: she hoped you could help the Farland Alliance carve out a trade route through Fraser's blockade.
...I'm truly sorry.
Until DisCity and the farlands establish formal diplomatic relations, I have no authority to send anyone in an official capacity. It would be seen as interference.
You paused briefly, watching for Helga's reaction. You had expected disappointment, perhaps even anger, but she simply raised an eyebrow.

steps.speaker: Helga
steps.content: I'm sitting right here, in the flesh. Isn't this formal enough?

Her question was posed as if it were the most natural thing in the world, with a disarmingly candid expression. You wondered for a moment if you were overthinking it; perhaps the farlanders simply dismissed formal protocol.
I appreciate that, but by the book...
test
test
test
test
test
test
This is the Bureau's visitor registry. If this were a formal diplomatic visit, I'd see your name on it.

steps.speaker: Helga
steps.content: Well, put it like that, and hardly a soul knows I'm in DisCity right now.
...Are you admitting that your Assembly doesn't know you're here?
Helga waves a hand, brushing the question aside.

steps.speaker: Helga
steps.content: Quit with the formal talk. You'll tie your tongue in knots, and it's wearing my ears out.

steps.speaker: Helga
steps.content: The Assembly... Bunch of windbags. Ever since we got free, all they do is yap themselves blue around a table.

steps.speaker: Helga
steps.content: I've heard enough noise. Time someone did something that actually needs doing.
Her decision to steer the conversation toward the Assembly and openly criticize its members had practically confirmed that her visit lacked official sanction.
However, a more pressing concern lingered: how had she managed to pinpoint this location and identify you personally?

Given that the farlands were still establishing themselves, it seemed highly unlikely they possessed the resources to place a spy. Nonetheless, the troubling possibility of a security breach within the Bureau gnawed at you.
You kept your questions to yourself for the moment. Helga went on.

steps.speaker: Helga
steps.content: Our lot won't take outside help. Call it "true self-reliance." Even with a ceasefire with DisCity, they aren't ready to shake hands with any Disian.

steps.speaker: Helga
steps.content: Heard the Fraser nobles are having a right laugh. Say we brought it on ourselves. That we're getting what we deserve.

steps.speaker: Helga
steps.content: But you gotta understand: Farlanders spent too many years living on someone else's say-so. Used when we were handy, tossed out like trash when we weren't. People are scared. And now Fraser has the gall to call us ungrateful.

steps.speaker: Helga
steps.content: Don't blame them, honestly. Everyone's been hurt too deep to trust easy. And hate? Yeah, I got plenty of that in me, too.
She fell silent for a moment, as if caught by a memory, but quickly shook her head.

steps.speaker: Helga
steps.content: But if we all just white-knuckle that hate, it's gonna dig a grave and push us all in.
Deep-seated beliefs don't change overnight. Same story here in DisCity.
Even people born with every advantage... Actually, especially them. That's often where the worst prejudices take root.
Just days ago, there were hate crimes against farland immigrants in Eastside.
A heavy sigh escaped Helga as she nodded in acknowledgment.

steps.speaker: Helga
steps.content: There'll always be folks carrying a grudge. But there are always folks with sense, too. Look, I'm here, right? Talking to you. That's gotta count for something.
Her casual tone was what finally drew the nagging question to the surface. You realized this was your moment to ask what you had wondered from the start.

options: How did you find out about the MBCC?

choices.text: How did you find out about the MBCC?

steps.content: But how did you, Speaker, even think to come to a place that... isn't exactly on the map?
The MBCC doesn't advertise. And for all you knew, I could've been just another Disian who holds hatred and prejudice toward the farlands.

steps.speaker: Helga
steps.content: I've got my sources, of course.
Noticing your furrowed brow, Helga burst into sudden, hearty laughter. The boisterous sound felt almost out of place in the stark interrogation room.

steps.speaker: Helga
steps.content: You've been sitting on that one a while, eh? Can't blame you. Chatting like this, I damn near forgot what sort of room I'm in.
After a perfunctory glance around the room, her gaze settled back on you. Her expression was now serious.

steps.speaker: Helga
steps.content: Don't fret. I'm not talking about spies, and no one's been leaking your secrets.

steps.speaker: Helga
steps.content: We've got a young researcher among us. Name's Hypatia. Sharp as a new pin. Says she knows you.

The story Rust had told you about that name came back to mind: she was once the young lady of the Campbell family, who took a path that diverged completely from her brother's. She had repeatedly defended the farlanders, eventually giving up her family name to stand with them.

steps.speaker: Helga
steps.content: She told me there's a place in DisCity called the Bureau of Crisis Control. That its Chief is a good sort. Gutsy, responsible.
I've heard of her. But I don't believe we've ever met directly.

steps.speaker: Helga
steps.content: But you'd know the name "Archivist 19260817," yeah?
As soon as the name reached you, a feeling stirred deep in your chest. You could almost hear the echo of keystrokes in the dead of night—you, alone before a glowing screen, typing with conviction.

steps.speaker: Helga
steps.content: She told me what the Chief once said to her: We farlanders will forge our own path. Find our own answers.

steps.speaker: Helga
steps.content: Without the Chief's trust back then, she never would've found the guts to expose Fraser's long game, even if it almost got her killed.
Is she... doing alright in the farlands now?

steps.speaker: Helga
steps.content: Some see a savior. Plenty still don't trust her. I mean, that bearing of hers screams Fraser nobility. The old hardliners in the Assembly are the worst. Convinced she's a spy, looking for any slip-up.
...She doesn't deserve that.

steps.speaker: Helga
steps.content: That's just the Farland Assembly for you these days.

steps.speaker: Helga
steps.content: Everyone's dug in, clinging to their grudges. Won't budge an inch. Talk a big game about the future, but don't spare a glance for the folks bleeding on the front lines.

steps.speaker: Helga
steps.content: I've seen that type before: sitting around big tables, deciding who lives and dies with a few words. I won't let our Assembly turn into that.
A faint undercurrent had stirred beneath her words. It might have been anger, sorrow, or disappointment. Yet the feeling was distant, its edges worn smooth, like river stones shaped by endless water.
You studied her. She appeared at ease, but a readiness was held in the line of her back, the tension in her core. Pale, old scars etched faint paths across her neck.
You're the current Speaker of the farlands, but you don't strike me as someone who sits behind a desk. If I had to guess... you were a soldier?
Helga nodded, a smile on her face.

steps.speaker: Helga
steps.content: Grew up in Fraser's refugee district. Served in their army for a good few years after. Though your spies in Fraser won't find a trace of me—Sorry. Old soldier's habit. I say what I think.

steps.speaker: Helga
steps.content: Fraser Army, 24th Company. I was their captain. After I deserted, command scrubbed us from the records. Simple as that, like we never happened.
You don't seem the type to desert under fire.

steps.speaker: Helga
steps.content: It was a suicide mission. Or rather, a mission to get my unit killed. Command called it a "grievous but necessary sacrifice."

steps.speaker: Helga
steps.content: To the brass, lives are numbers. War's a game. They've never set foot on the line. Never seen the kids in the med tents, blown to pieces.

steps.speaker: Helga
steps.content: Heh. They're too soft for that. The sight would ruin their appetites for a week.
A cold laugh escaped her before her expression hardened, her gaze fixing intently on you.

steps.speaker: Helga
steps.content: But I have.

steps.speaker: Helga
steps.content: That's why I only trust the kids on the front lines. Doesn't matter where they're from.

steps.speaker: Helga
steps.content: I trust Hypatia. I've seen how she fights for our people. So I wanted to meet you myself, the one who said those words to her.

steps.speaker: Helga
steps.content: I'm not here for the Assembly. And I've got nothing to trade you. Just think of it as a personal ask, from one regular farlander to someone who might be a friend worth trusting.
With that, she shook her head, a knowing smile on her face.

steps.speaker: Helga
steps.content: I know it sounds damn foolish. To your DisCity politicians, this must seem downright childish.

steps.speaker: Helga
steps.content: But then, I was never much of a proper leader. Here I am, my age, and I can't even keep my own Assembly in line.

steps.speaker: Helga
steps.content: Childish, foolish—call it what you want. I just want to do right by the people around me.
When she finished, she simply held your gaze. In her eyes, you could see the echoes of many familiar faces.
In that moment, you knew you could not refuse her.
Funny. "Childish." "Foolish." I hear those words aimed at me a lot, too.
You gently set aside the documents in your hands.
I can't act as the Chief officially. But then, I can also just be a person. If there's anything I can do to help, I will.
So, let me introduce myself again. Please, call me ${PlayerName}.

steps.speaker: Helga
steps.content: Just Helga is fine.

You stood and opened the interrogation room door, motioning for her to go ahead. Helga got to her feet, smoothing her lapels and adjusting her coat. Her posture was rigid—shoulders squared, back rod-straight—the unmistakable carriage of someone with military training.
—Or, as she herself had put it, not a soldier. A deserter.
That military experience you mentioned. I'm curious. Is it a long story?

steps.speaker: Helga
steps.content: Yeah. It's a long one alright...
That's fine. We've got time on the way.
[Alsa Highlands]

Following the planned route along the windswept cliffs of Alsa Highlands, you and Helga place the explosive charges with methodical precision. At the seventh emplacement, as you set the device, a sharp sting bites into your fingertip.
...Hngh!
Your hand recoils from the soil. Jutting from the dirt is a jagged sliver of metal. You carefully work it free and wipe the grime from its surface with your sleeve.

steps.speaker: Helga
steps.content: A Fraser Third Class Merit. One of the cooks in my unit had one just like it.

steps.speaker: Helga
steps.content: Used to be a machine gunner, till a bullet took his leg. Command wanted him discharged. He refused. Said he'd only ever done odd jobs before the army, had no family to speak of; a cripple going back meant no one would take him. So they stuck him in the mess instead.

steps.speaker: Helga
steps.content: This medal was the most valuable thing he ever owned. Look at it now. Rusted to hell.
You lift the forlorn medal, turning its face to the weak sun. The design etched upon it has been worn away by time and touch, rendered a mystery.

steps.speaker: Helga
steps.content: Fraser never sent reinforcements. From the start, they meant for us to die here, to hand the position over. It was a deal they'd struck. Everyone knew. Everyone but me.

steps.speaker: Helga
steps.content: Or maybe... I did know. I just refused to believe it.

steps.speaker: Helga
steps.content: Refused to believe the skills I was so damn proud of meant nothing to Fraser's brass. Refused to believe the glory and the life I thought I'd earned... were never meant for me at all.
The sun burns low and immense, a smearing glare that blurs the world.
Against that vast, untouchable light, the only tangible thing left is the weight of the rusted medal in your hand.
This is also where you made contact with Mania.
With a silent nod, Helga takes the medal from your hand. Her eyes fall to the ground, fixing on the blackened earth where blood soaked deep into the soil long ago.

steps.speaker: Helga
steps.content: I thought fate would be fair. So many died because of me. What right did I have to live? But not only did I live... I came out seeing clearer than ever.

steps.speaker: Helga
steps.content: Every bone, every drop of blood my friends left behind... I can see it all, crystal clear. I became exactly what Fraser needed. The old me would've been over the damn moon...
Her fingers close into a hard fist. There's a soft, brittle crunch as the rust-weakened metal folds in her grip.
So, is this the ending you want to tell?
She stands motionless, head bowed, as the oppressive darkness moans around her.
Then, her gun snaps up toward you.
Bang!
The gunshot cuts the air, silencing the whimper. A Corruptor tumbles backward into the pit.
And in the wake of the shot, the trench beneath you erupts. The shadows boil, and a forest of twisted, clawing arms reaches up from the depths.

steps.speaker: Helga
steps.content: ...They're awake. We need to move. How many left?
Four.
You force a quicker pace, but reality itself seems to decay faster. From the depths below, a wave of dark, Mania-charged mist erupts, plunging the highlands into a frigid twilight instantly.
A cold deeper than ice penetrates your skin. The Mania readings are off the scale. Helga's warning echoes in your mind: delay any longer, and the outpost will be next.

Corruptors lunge from the murk, forcing you to a crawl. Helga's covering fire is a desperate staccato, but you see the toll the mist is taking: her reloads are fumbled, her aim growing heavy and slow.

steps.speaker: Helga
steps.content: ...Behind you!!!
You spin around to find a Corruptor towering at your back.
Just as its limb whistles down, the air solidifies into a wall of familiar blue light, shielding you from the danger.
It's the defensive field from the anti-Mania device you left with Milonn.

The field's disruptive pulse staggers the surrounding Corruptors, buying a precious second. That's all the time a lithe, fast-moving figure needs to plant herself before you, her spear sweeping out in a defiant crescent.

steps.speaker: Tavera
steps.content: Back off!!!
The farland warrior strikes with ferocity, a single kick sending the Corruptor tumbling back into the pit. She plants her spear and takes a protective stance before you.
Her gaze flickers back, her body instinctively edging away. Her lips part, then close. After a pause, she finally speaks:

steps.speaker: Tavera
steps.content: ...According to the Speaker's original plan, I'm to guard you.
From close by, Vester's scoff carries over the chaos. He fights beside Helga, his scimitar flashing in a clean, lethal arc that splits a Corruptor. With the creature falling, he adds:

steps.speaker: Vester
steps.content: Milonn lost his nerve. Didn't think we'd make it out alone, so he came scrambling after you... Hmph, fear's rotted his brains.

steps.speaker: Milonn
steps.content: ...That's why I had to follow! They gave me the gear to survive... They're my only chance to make it out alive!

steps.speaker: Vester
steps.content: And Tavera? Insists on following the Speaker. "Loyalty." She uses that word very... selectively.

steps.speaker: Tavera
steps.content: Everything I know about fighting, the Speaker taught me... If she tells me to fight beside a Disian... then fine. This once.

steps.speaker: Vester
steps.content: Heh. So it seems I'm the only one left out in the cold.
With that said, his scimitar whips out to fell another foe.

steps.speaker: Vester
steps.content: Go on, laugh, Helga. When we get back, I'll be sure to give the Assembly a full report. Every last detail.

steps.speaker: Helga
steps.content: Do it. Tell them how we cleared the Alsa Highlands and put a wrench in Fraser's plans.
She pauses, her gaze shifting to the young person nearby.

steps.speaker: Helga
steps.content: And be sure to tell them ${PlayerName} helped us. You remember that name. You hear me?
After a final, scathing look at Helga, Vester vanishes back into the storm of combat. His style is unmistakable: swift, precise, and brutal cuts that speak of a seasoned warrior.
Your path is cleared by their desperate fight, allowing you to reach the last demolition point at last. But the area is already submerged in a dense, corrosive fog of Mania.
The Mania contamination is too dense. They can't pass through.
A single look passes between you. Helga reads your intent instantly. Before you can move, her hand is on your arm, fingers closing tight enough to stop you.

steps.speaker: Helga
steps.content: You've done more than enough for the farlands already.
No... this isn't just for the farlands. Isn't it the same for you?
The truth is, I don't remember my own past. I've never done any of this out of loyalty to a city, or to some higher-up. It was never about that.
But even so... there are people I care about. People I trust. They come from everywhere, and they'll go everywhere, walking their own paths.
You said it yourself, Helga. The road ahead is long. So...
I just have to keep moving forward.
You take a final breath and leap into the churning Mania below.
A frigid, viscous presence swallows you. Countless spectral hands claw at your limbs, dragging you toward the abyss. The world dissolves into a chorus of maddened whispers—
Why me... Why does it have to be me... I don't want to die... I want to go home!
Kill! Kill them! Kill every last one!
I'm still young... Am I...? We shouldn't have known only this... They taught us nothing but killing!
It was the only way... the only path to the future they promised...
That place... Will there be a place for me there, Mom?
You're adults. Please, tell us the answer.
Who were <color=#fb9259>they</color>? Whose children? Whose friends? Whose lovers?
Who could <color=#fb9259>they</color> have been?
Bang!
A bullet grazes the air beside your head, yet you're untouched.
Behind you, Helga lands almost in sync, rifle already rising to her shoulder—a motion polished across countless battlefields.
Each round she fires is a calculated denial, keeping the lunging Corruptors at bay.
All you have to do is run. Forward. Only forward.
So, is this how the story ends?

steps.speaker: Helga
steps.content: No. This is not the end.

Another shot, and then the rifle falls silent, its magazine spent. Without pause, Helga's hand finds a fresh one, the reload a seamless ritual. The weapon barks back to life, carving a safe passage forward for the young one.

steps.speaker: Helga
steps.content: When I finally dragged myself back to Fraser, to the streets I knew... folks were still living worse than dogs. And way off in the distance, that golden palace was still shining, bright as ever.

steps.speaker: Helga
steps.content: We were gone so long, but not a damn thing changed. Like we never even lived.

steps.speaker: Helga
steps.content: I can't stop wondering what you'd all be like if you'd made it. Made it to thirty, or forty. I try to picture it... but I can't. And that eats at me.

steps.speaker: Helga
steps.content: I swore I'd kill every last one of 'em in the Senate. Kill them all, even if it killed me too...

steps.speaker: Helga
steps.content: But I can't die. You all told me to keep living, so I did. Lived a long time now. In a world like this, how many get to my age? I owe you all for that.

steps.speaker: Helga
steps.content: So I listened. I'll live. I have to live.
The young man doesn't glance behind. He becomes a blur of motion, legs driving him forward with a speed that seems to outpace the bullets.
steps.female_content: The young woman doesn't glance behind. She becomes a blur of motion, legs driving her forward with a speed that seems to outpace the bullets.

steps.content: Keep up with him, Helga tells herself. This time, keep up.
steps.female_content: Keep up with her, Helga tells herself. This time, keep up.

steps.speaker: Helga
steps.content: So I kept on living. Met all sorts along the way. So many remind me of you. The good parts, sure, but the stubborn streaks even more... Thinking of that, I just can't stay mad at them.
He stumbles forward, and for a moment, his silhouette merges with the memory of theirs.
steps.female_content: She stumbles forward, and for a moment, her silhouette merges with the memory of theirs.

steps.speaker: Helga
steps.content: It finally clicked... so many kids in this world are just like you. And they'll be everywhere, always.
One could ask him a thousand times why he presses on, and hear a thousand different answers. But behind them all lies the same truth:
steps.female_content: One could ask her a thousand times why she presses on, and hear a thousand different answers. But behind them all lies the same truth:

steps.content: Because there is still something in this world worth hoping for.

steps.speaker: Helga
steps.content: Yeah... I've lived a long life. It'll end one day.

steps.speaker: Helga
steps.content: Fraser, DisCity, these farland camps, all those little towns I never heard of... they'll all be gone someday too.

steps.speaker: Helga
steps.content: ...But even then, someone'll still be walking this road.
Reload. Aim. Fire. Again.

steps.speaker: Helga
steps.content: Before I'm too old to go on, I'll make sure these kids keep walking, straight on forever! I'll make damn sure this road never ends!
One more shot. The Corruptor ahead convulses and falls silent, its form parting the viscous gloom like a curtain.
—You're there. The last charge is set. You turn, and the soft beep in your ear begins its fatal cadence.
You can't stop yet. Your body screams—fire in the chest, grating joints, salt in the eyes—but you run.
Behind you, the world erupts.
The blast swallows sound. Yet the rugged highland terrain beneath your feet firms into an unnatural smoothness, as if a road laid down by the fallen.
It carries you, steadfast, through the rain of cinders.
<size=44><color=#fb9259>Alsa Highlands has been purified.</color></size>
But you must not stop. You run, with everything you have, until—

Until it feels as though you have run through four decades in one gasping moment. The mist dissolves, and sunlight reveals the elder woman before you: her hair returning to its youthful hue, her scars fading from sight.
Until you are looking into eyes that are young again, alight with a hope not yet worn down by years.
The young woman with frayed sleeves offers a hand and pulls you up.
Her lips part, and she speaks.
"I wish you a long road ahead."
